title: Sandy Beaches in Fažana, Croatia: What's Real in 2027
metaDescription: Fažana has no true sandy beach: Pineta, Valbandon and Bi Val are pebble and concrete. Where the nearest real sand is, with travel times and kid tips.
content:
## Does Fažana Have a Sandy Beach?

No. Fažana's shoreline is pebble, fine gravel and poured concrete, like most of Istria. The closest thing to sand inside the municipality is a sandy section at Bi Val and a shallow sandbar zone at Valbandon. Neither is a proper sand beach. Travellers who need soft sand for toddlers or sandcastles should plan day trips south toward Medulin and Premantura.

## Beach Surface in Fažana, Beach by Beach

### Valbandon (public beach), fine pebble and concrete
Valbandon, about 2 km south of the centre, is the best compromise for families. The surface mixes small smooth pebbles with concrete sunbathing platforms. One section is enclosed by a sandbar, with shallow water and a soft entry that suits small children. Pine trees give natural shade along the back of the beach, and it is lifeguarded. A coastal promenade links it to Fažana, so walking or cycling is easier than driving. The stones can be uneven in places, so water shoes help.

### MUP Valbandon, gravel, pebble and concrete
This is the longest and largest beach in the Valbandon area and is popular with locals. Gravel, pebble and concrete zones sit side by side, and a few piers make entering deeper water easy. It is more of a swimming and sunbathing beach than a paddling one. It tends to be less crowded than the town beaches.

### Pineta, gravel and pebble
Pineta lies about 2 km from Fažana and about 7 km from Pula, next to the campsite. It is a long gravel and pebble beach with some concrete platforms, under pines. It is lifeguarded, has showers and toilets, and has large parking. Entry is gradual, so it works for non-swimmers and children. Shade is the best of the Fažana beaches here, but there is no sand.

### Bi Val (Bi Village), pebble with sandy parts
Bi Val is the one place in Fažana where sand is mentioned at all. It is a long pebble beach with some sandy patches, a gradual entry, and a marked swimming zone. It is inside a campsite complex, so check the access rules before going if you are not staying there. Sunbeds, parasols, showers and changing cabins are available.

### Town beaches (Stara Fažana / north beach and the south beach near the children's playground)
Both are pebble or gravel and close to the old town and harbour. The north beach is a pebble bay about 300 m long. The south beach, by the playground, has deep pine shade. They are convenient for a short swim but are the busiest in July and August.

## Nearest Real Sandy Beaches

### Bijeca, Medulin (about 30–40 minutes)
Bijeca is the usual answer for sand near Pula. The seabed is sand mixed with fine gravel, and the water stays shallow for a long way out, which is why families choose it. Drive south through Pula toward Medulin, about 30–40 minutes in normal traffic. Expect crowds and a paid or limited parking situation in peak summer; arrive before 10:00.

### Pješčana uvala, Premantura area (about 35–45 minutes)
The name means "sandy bay". It has a shallow, sandy entry and is a quieter option than Medulin. It is close to Cape Kamenjak, where the other beaches are rocky or pebble. Take water shoes if you plan to explore beyond the sandy bay.

### Why not look further?
True wide sand beaches in Croatia, such as Lopar on Rab, are many hours away with a ferry. For a day trip from Fažana, Medulin is the only sensible choice.

## Which Fažana Beach Is Best for Small Children?

Valbandon's sandbar section and Pineta's gradual entry are the safest. Both are lifeguarded. Bi Val is the third option because of its sandy parts and marked swimming zone. Avoid concrete-edge entry points with toddlers; the step off the slab can be abrupt.

## Practical Tips

- Fažana is about 9 km from Pula, so combining a morning at Valbandon with an afternoon at Medulin is realistic.
- Take the promenade to Valbandon or Pineta instead of driving; parking is limited on hot weekends.
- Pack water shoes for every pebble beach here.
- Go before 10:00 in July and August for shade under the pines.
- Weekday mornings are calmest; the town beaches fill after the Brijuni boats return.

## Verdict: Is Fažana Right for Sand Lovers?

Not as a base. Anyone whose holiday depends on sand under their feet should stay in Medulin or Premantura instead. Don't pay extra for a Fažana apartment advertised as "near the sandy beach"; that description does not fit any beach here. Fažana suits travellers who accept fine pebble, pine shade, calm shallow water and the Brijuni ferry, and who treat Bijeca as an occasional day trip.

faq.question: Is there a sandy beach in Fažana?
faq.answer: No. Fažana's beaches are pebble, gravel and concrete. Bi Val has some sandy patches and Valbandon has a small sandbar area, but neither is a true sand beach.

faq.question: Where is the nearest sandy beach to Fažana?
faq.answer: Bijeca in Medulin is the most popular, about 30–40 minutes by car. Pješčana uvala near Premantura is a quieter sandy alternative, about 35–45 minutes away.

faq.question: Which Fažana beach is best for toddlers?
faq.answer: Valbandon, with its shallow sandbar-protected section, and Pineta, with its gradual entry, are the best choices. Both are lifeguarded and have pine shade.

faq.question: Do I need water shoes in Fažana?
faq.answer: Yes, especially at Valbandon and MUP, where stones can be uneven. Water shoes also help on the concrete-to-sea steps.

faq.question: Can I walk to the beaches from Fažana town?
faq.answer: Yes. A coastal promenade connects Fažana with Pineta (about 2 km) and Valbandon (about 2 km). Walking or cycling avoids the parking problem in peak season.

faq.question: Is a Medulin day trip from Fažana worth it?
faq.answer: Yes, if sand matters to you. The drive is about 30–40 minutes, and an early start avoids the worst crowds and parking trouble.

quickAnswer: Fažana has no true sandy beach. Its beaches (Pineta, Valbandon, MUP, Bi Val, town beaches) are pebble, fine gravel and concrete, with only small sandy patches at Bi Val and a sandbar at Valbandon. The nearest real sand is around Medulin and Premantura, roughly 30–40 minutes by car.
